source.title: Dissecting the Effects of SGD Noise in Distinct Regimes of Deep Learning
source.authors: Antonio Sclocchi; M. Geiger; M. Wyart

record.file_problem: None; the supplied text contains the full paper and appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports its own test-error results as SGD noise changes and argues that the effect depends on training regime, with non-monotonic outcomes and a dynamical explanation. It does not test the specific interventions in the listed versions.
record.gate_note: The study varies SGD temperature, initialization scale, and training-set size, then reports held-out test error, weight variation, and training time. Its test-error values are supplied mainly as figures; cited studies' results are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study measures how SGD temperature, initialization scale and training-set size affect generalization and training dynamics, but does not test V1–V8. In particular, varying learning rate at small batch sizes and training to zero hinge loss does not test V5's large-batch effect under fixed epoch budgets. Weight displacement and the argument about flat hinge-loss minima do not measure V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or its correlation with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find regime-dependent benefits and harms from SGD noise and propose that noise increases non-informative weights, requiring informative weights to grow further and delaying complete fitting. They connect crossover temperatures to training-set size through dynamical scaling laws, while leaving the sign of the performance effect and its dependence on architecture and data structure unresolved.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies SGD temperature T = η/B and initialization scale, and trains with hinge loss until zero training loss; it reports that cross-entropy with early stopping gives the same power-law dependencies. It does not test the listed version-specific interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-error response varies with initialization regime, SGD temperature, architecture, dataset, and training-set size. In the feature regime, CNN test-error curves change shape with P; the authors state Tc cannot always be extracted from test-error curves.

fits_no_version.finding: Held-out error responds to SGD temperature in regime-dependent, sometimes non-monotonic ways; improvement crossovers can align across training-set sizes when expressed through relative weight displacement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The effect of SGD noise on generalization depends on initialization regime, architecture and training-set size.

fits_no_version.finding: Relative weight displacement and training time exhibit power-law dependence on SGD temperature and training-set size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD noise affects late training dynamics, increasing weight growth and delaying complete fitting.

fits_no_version.finding: The teacher-student perceptron's non-informative weight norm scales with temperature independently of training-set size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD noise increases non-informative weight components, requiring larger informative weights to fit the data.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 202, 2023
record.problems: Test-error findings are primarily presented in figures without numerical values in the text. The paper notes that the sign of the SGD-noise effect and its relation to data structure and architecture remain open. Exponent-fit error is around ±0.2.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted. Other reported training-time and weight-variation scaling results across additional architecture and dataset combinations are not separately enumerated beyond the selected conditions.

untested.parts: No random-label fitting and natural-versus-random-label held-out comparison.
No width sweep beyond the width required for zero training error.
No direct assessment of the convolutional advantage over fully connected architectures or the contribution of local connectivity; reporting both architectures does not establish that comparison.
No large-batch performance comparison under fixed epoch budgets or test of recipes that remove that penalty.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement, correlation with generalization gaps, or ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
No removal of highly memorized examples versus matched random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All rows retain versions=['none']. Their cannot_determine states concern the listed claim versions, not whether the paper observes its reported temperature and dynamical effects. The paper's criticism of a static flatness explanation does not specifically refute V7's correlational, magnitude-aware claim.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or comparison of natural-label and random-label test accuracy.
No width sweep past the interpolation threshold.
No controlled convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison of test error on the same image task.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
No large-batch comparison at a fixed epoch budget; batch size is small, and the paper varies the ratio of learning rate to batch size.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.

rows.subject: 5-hidden-layers fully-connected network (FC)
rows.stage_stated: trained until hinge loss is zero
rows.operation_detail: Test error across SGD temperatures in the lazy regime
rows.measure: Test error as a function of SGD temperature T
rows.value: Test error initially slightly degrades, then improves before Tmax; improving crossover Tc depends on P and is approximately Tc ∼ P −0.5.
rows.note: The paper describes the trend and crossover in text; the precise test-error values are figure-only.
rows.check: The reported non-monotonic temperature response is supported, but does not measure any listed version; partial is not a version-relative state here.

rows.subject: 9-hidden-layers CNN (MNAS architecture)
rows.stage_stated: trained until hinge loss is zero
rows.operation_detail: Test error across SGD temperatures in the lazy regime
rows.measure: Test error as a function of SGD temperature T
rows.value: Test error degrades as T increases, then improves for larger P near Tmax; the curve is non-monotonic and its shape changes with P.
rows.note: The paper states the trend and changing curve shape; precise test-error values are figure-only.
rows.check: The lazy-regime result is supported by Figure 3 with B=16. Figure 1(b) instead uses B=64, and Figure 16(a) concerns feature learning; these should not be combined under this row's conditions. No listed version is measured.

rows.subject: fully connected neural network
rows.stage_stated: trained until hinge loss is zero
rows.operation_detail: Test error across SGD temperatures in the feature-learning regime
rows.measure: Test error as a function of SGD temperature T
rows.value: Test error starts improving at a crossover temperature depending on P; the reported fit is Tc ∼ P −0.7.
rows.note: The paper reports the crossover and fit in text and caption; precise test-error values are figure-only.
rows.check: The crossover scaling is supported, but does not measure any listed version. The task is binary MNIST parity classification.

rows.subject: CNN (MNAS architecture)
rows.stage_stated: trained until hinge loss is zero
rows.operation_detail: Test error across SGD temperatures in the feature-learning regime
rows.measure: Test error as a function of SGD temperature T
rows.value: Test error improves more significantly with T as P increases; curves have different shapes and cannot be matched by rescaling the x-axis.
rows.note: The caption states the qualitative trend and limitation; precise test-error values are figure-only.
rows.check: The qualitative temperature response is supported, but does not measure any listed version. The task is binary CIFAR-10 animals-versus-rest classification.

rows.subject: 5-hidden-layers fully-connected network (FC)
rows.stage_stated: trained until hinge loss is zero
rows.operation_detail: Relate test error to relative weight variation across training-set sizes
rows.measure: Test error plotted against relative weight variation
rows.value: Plotting test error against relative weight variation aligns the point where test error starts improving across P.
rows.note: The text describes the alignment; no numerical test-error values are stated.
rows.check: The alignment is supported. Relative displacement from initialization is not magnitude-aware sharpness or a generalization-gap measurement.

rows.subject: CNN (MNAS architecture)

rows.note: The paper describes approximate alignment; no numerical test-error values are stated.
rows.check: The approximate alignment is supported. Relative displacement from initialization does not test V7 or another listed version.

rows.subject: 5-hidden-layers fully-connected network (FC)
rows.stage_stated: trained until hinge loss is zero
rows.operation_detail: Measure relative weight variation against SGD temperature and training-set size
rows.measure: Relative weight variation at the end of training
rows.value: ∆w ∼ T δ P γ, with γ ≈ 0.4 and δ ≈ 1.
rows.note: The reported relationship is an empirical scaling of weight variation, not a sharpness measure.
rows.check: The scaling values are supported, but weight displacement does not measure any listed version.

rows.subject: 5-hidden-layers fully-connected network (FC)
rows.stage_stated: trained until hinge loss is zero
rows.operation_detail: Measure training time against SGD temperature and training-set size
rows.value: t∗ ∼ T P b, with b around 1.3.
rows.note: The paper defines t∗ as learning rate times the number of steps required to bring hinge loss to zero.
rows.check: The training-time scaling is supported. Training to zero loss with variable duration does not measure V5's held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.

rows.subject: perceptron
rows.stage_stated: trained until hinge loss is zero
rows.operation_detail: Measure orthogonal weight component against SGD temperature and training-set size
rows.measure: Norm of non-informative weights at end of training, ||w⊥||
rows.value: ||w⊥|| ∼ T and is independent of P.
rows.note: This is a toy perceptron result offered as a test of the proposed effect of T on the non-informative component.
rows.check: The perceptron result is supported, but non-informative weight growth does not measure any listed version.
